title: Failed Class 6. Built a company worth thousands of crores anyway. October 25, 2026.
excerpt: From a poet whose lyrics outlived him, to a Chandigarh-born diplomat now representing Canada in the Gulf, to a doctor who spent four decades flying between two countries to run free surgery camps, to a Kerala port outpacing ports a decade older, to a school dropout who built a food empire - October 25's five stories are about what gets built when someone refuses to accept where they started.
bodyHtml:
Every story today starts with a setback - a death that didn't end a legacy, a classroom in Chandigarh that led to an embassy, a car accident that didn't stop four decades of surgery camps, a port with no track record, and a sixth-grade failure that became a food company worth thousands of crores.

October 25, 1980: Hindi cinema's most literary lyricist died at 58 - mid-conversation, playing cards with friends

Sahir Ludhianvi, born Abdul Hayee in Ludhiana in 1921, died of a heart attack in Mumbai on October 25, 1980. He wrote some of Hindi film's most enduring lyrics, bringing the weight of Urdu progressive poetry into mainstream Bollywood songwriting, and was awarded the Padma Shri in 1971.

He left Chandigarh at 19 for a Canadian university. In 2026, he became Canada's Ambassador to the UAE

Angad Singh Dhillon, born in Chandigarh, was named Canada's Ambassador to the United Arab Emirates on September 25, 2026, after a career built inside Canada's federal government and the Prime Minister's Office.

He spent half of every year in the US, and half running free surgery camps across India

Dr. Sharad Kumar Dixit, who emigrated from Maharashtra to the US in 1959, founded "The India Project" in 1968, personally performing over 65,000 free cleft lip, cleft palate and eye surgeries across India over four decades - continuing even after a 1978 car accident left him wheelchair-bound.

A Kerala port just became one of the fastest in the world to hit 1,000 ships

Vizhinjam International Seaport received its 1,000th commercial vessel in June 2026, less than two years after its first commercial call - alongside Indian port records for container volume and ultra-large vessel calls.

Failed Class 6. Left school to work the coffee plantations. Built a company worth thousands of crores anyway

P.C. Mustafa grew up in a remote Wayanad village with no roads or electricity, failed Class 6, and dropped out - until a teacher convinced his parents to send him back. In 2005 he pooled 25,000 rupees with five cousins to start iD Fresh Food, now valued in the thousands of crores.

Five stories, one pattern: a poet's death that didn't end his influence, a classroom in Punjab that led to an embassy in Abu Dhabi, a car accident that didn't stop forty years of surgery camps, a two-year-old port outpacing ports a decade older, and a sixth-grade dropout who built an empire anyway.
